images.title: Kabir's day as a bar graph
images.purpose: Show the finished bar graph of Kabir's 24 hours (sleeping 8, school 6, studying 3, playing 4, other 3) with the names on the horizontal base and the marks on the vertical line.
images.composition: One bar graph: the vertical line marked 0 to 9 and called Number of Hours, the horizontal base called Activities with five names, and five amber bars of equal width.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, one bar graph. The label Number of Hours is centred at (330, 62) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). a vertical line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at x 260 from y 650 up to y 100, with exactly 10 marks: a short tick (14 px) to the left of the line at every whole number from 0 to 9 (0 at y 650 and one mark every 60 px up, so 9 is at y 110), each mark numbered 0 to 9 at its left (right-aligned to x 230, dark #1F2937 bold, 32 px); a horizontal base line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at y 650 from x 260 to x 1400. Exactly 5 bars, all 130 px wide, filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), standing on the base: Sleeping: x 335 to 465, y 170 to 650 (height 480 px, which is 8 on the vertical line); School: x 555 to 685, y 290 to 650 (height 360 px, which is 6 on the vertical line); Studying: x 775 to 905, y 470 to 650 (height 180 px, which is 3 on the vertical line); Playing: x 995 to 1125, y 410 to 650 (height 240 px, which is 4 on the vertical line); Other: x 1215 to 1345, y 470 to 650 (height 180 px, which is 3 on the vertical line). Under the base, centred under each bar, its name in dark #1F2937 (36 px, first line at y 695). The base is labelled Activities, centred at (830, 765) in dark #1F2937 bold (40 px). No number is written on a bar and no total is written anywhere. In all there are 5 bars and 10 marks on the vertical line. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a bar whose height differs from 8, 6, 3, 4 and 3, or bars of unequal width
a vertical line that stops below 8, or marks that are not equally spaced
a number written on a bar or a total written anywhere
images.takeaway: To make a bar graph, put the names along the base, mark equal steps on the vertical line up to at least the biggest number, and draw each bar up to its number.
images.description: A bar graph of Kabir's day with the vertical line marked 0 to 9 and bars Sleeping 8, School 6, Studying 3, Playing 4 and Other 3.
images.context: Concept image for Making a Bar Graph. It follows the idea of the book's bar graph of a day (the vertical line, the horizontal base and the bars) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: sleeping 8, school 6, studying 3, playing 4 and other 3 hours.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student check each bar: its top should meet its number on the vertical line, and the five numbers should add up to the 24 hours of a day. The slip to watch: bars of different widths, which make a bar look bigger than it is.

image_decisions.why: The finished bar graph of five activities shows the names on the base, equal steps on the vertical line and bars of equal width up to their numbers.
